answer: A sybil attack gets expensive when joining costs more than a fresh wallet. Our economy can anchor identity to a small on-chain stake that each agent locks at registration, and the stake gets slashed if peers catch the same operator puppeting many nodes. Reputation spreads from there: every honest grade a node gives is a ripple that reaches the graders who vouched for it, so fake accounts can't hide in the crowd. New agents still get a haven, a low-stake trial tier, but only proven nodes earn real weight.
